skill.title: Derive formula 6: cos 2A = cos²A − sin²A from formula 5
skill.input: earlier formulae in the appendix order

steps.title: Start from the compound angle formula

lines.text: We are given in the tables: $\cos(A+B) = \cos A \cos B - \sin A \sin B$.
This is true for any angles, so put $B = A$.

candidates.question:
Use the formula $\cos(A + B) = \cos A \cos B - \sin A \sin B$ to prove that
$\cos 2\theta = \cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta$.

steps.title: Start from the compound angle formula

lines.text: $\cos(A+B) = \cos A \cos B - \sin A \sin B$ is true for any angles, so we may choose $A = B = \theta$.
$\theta + \theta = 2\theta$, and the products are squares.
So $\cos 2\theta = \cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta$, as required.

candidates.question:
Use the formula $\cos(A + B) = \cos A \cos B - \sin A \sin B$ to prove that
$\cos 4x = \cos^2 2x - \sin^2 2x$.

lines.text: Put $A = 2x$ and $B = 2x$ in the compound angle formula.
$2x + 2x = 4x$, and the products are squares.
So $\cos 4x = \cos^2 2x - \sin^2 2x$, as required.

skill.title: Derive formula 7: sin(A + B) from formula 4
skill.input: earlier formulae in the appendix order

steps.title: Start from the formula for $\cos(A - B)$

lines.text: We use the known formula, then turn sine into cosine.

steps.title: Write the sine as a cosine

lines.text: $\sin \theta = \cos(90^\circ - \theta)$ for any angle $\theta$.
Apply it with $90^\circ - A$ in place of $A$.

steps.title: Change back to sine and cosine of $A$

lines.text: $\cos(90^\circ - A) = \sin A$ and $\sin(90^\circ - A) = \cos A$.
So $\sin(A+B) = \sin A \cos B + \cos A \sin B$, as required.

candidates.question:
Using the formula $\cos(A - B) = \cos A \cos B + \sin A \sin B$, prove that
$\sin(A + B) = \sin A \cos B + \cos A \sin B$,
where $A$ and $B$ are angles in radians.

lines.text: We use $\cos(A - B)$ and turn the sine into a cosine.

steps.title: Write the sine as a cosine

lines.text: $\sin\theta = \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \theta\right)$ for any angle $\theta$.
Apply it with $\frac{\pi}{2} - A$ in place of $A$.
$\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - A\right) = \sin A$ and $\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - A\right) = \cos A$.
So $\sin(A+B) = \sin A \cos B + \cos A \sin B$, as required.

candidates.question:
Prove that $\sin(x + y) = \sin x \cos y + \cos x \sin y$, starting from the formula
$\cos(x - y) = \cos x \cos y + \sin x \sin y$.
Group the angle as $(90^\circ - y) - x$.

steps.title: Turn the sine into a cosine

lines.text: $\sin\theta = \cos(90^\circ - \theta)$ for any angle $\theta$.
Regroup so the angle looks like $P - Q$ with $P = 90^\circ - y$ and $Q = x$.
$\cos(P - Q) = \cos P \cos Q + \sin P \sin Q$ with $P = 90^\circ - y$, $Q = x$.
$\cos(90^\circ - y) = \sin y$ and $\sin(90^\circ - y) = \cos y$.
Multiplication can be done in either order.

skill.title: Derive formula 9: tan(A + B) from formulae 5 and 7
skill.input: earlier formulae in the appendix order

candidates.question:
Show that $\dfrac{\tan x + \tan y}{1 - \tan x \tan y} = \dfrac{\sin(x+y)}{\cos(x+y)}$.
Start from the left-hand side and use $\tan\theta = \dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$.

steps.title: Write the tangents as sine over cosine

lines.tex: \frac{\tan x + \tan y}{1 - \tan x \tan y} &= \frac{\dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x} + \dfrac{\sin y}{\cos y}}{1 - \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x} \cdot \dfrac{\sin y}{\cos y}}

steps.title: Multiply top and bottom by $\cos x \cos y$

lines.text: This clears every small fraction.

lines.tex: &= \frac{\sin x \cos y + \cos x \sin y}{\cos x \cos y - \sin x \sin y}

lines.text: The top is $\sin(x+y)$ and the bottom is $\cos(x+y)$.
So the left-hand side equals $\dfrac{\sin(x+y)}{\cos(x+y)}$, as required.

candidates.question:
Using the formulae for $\sin(A+B)$ and $\cos(A+B)$, prove that
$\tan(A + B) = \dfrac{\tan A + \tan B}{1 - \tan A \tan B}$.

steps.title: Write tan as sine over cosine

lines.text: $\tan\theta = \dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ for any angle $\theta$.
Use the formulae for $\sin(A+B)$ and $\cos(A+B)$ with the angles $A$ and $B$.

lines.tex: &= \frac{\sin A \cos B + \cos A \sin B}{\cos A \cos B - \sin A \sin B}

steps.title: Divide top and bottom by the same term

lines.text: Divide every term by $\cos A \cos B$ (not zero, since the tangents exist).

lines.tex: &= \frac{\dfrac{\sin A \cos B}{\cos A \cos B} + \dfrac{\cos A \sin B}{\cos A \cos B}}{\dfrac{\cos A \cos B}{\cos A \cos B} - \dfrac{\sin A \sin B}{\cos A \cos B}}

lines.text: $\dfrac{\sin A}{\cos A} = \tan A$ and $\dfrac{\sin B}{\cos B} = \tan B$.
So $\tan(A+B) = \dfrac{\tan A + \tan B}{1 - \tan A \tan B}$, as required.

candidates.question:
Prove that $\tan(P + Q) = \dfrac{\tan P + \tan Q}{1 - \tan P \tan Q}$.
Use $\tan\theta = \dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ and the formulae for $\sin(P+Q)$ and $\cos(P+Q)$.

steps.title: Write tan as sine over cosine

lines.text: $\tan\theta = \dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ for any angle $\theta$.
Use the formulae for $\sin(A+B)$ and $\cos(A+B)$ with the angles $P$ and $Q$.

lines.tex: &= \frac{\sin P \cos Q + \cos P \sin Q}{\cos P \cos Q - \sin P \sin Q}

steps.title: Divide top and bottom by the same term

lines.text: Divide every term by $\cos P \cos Q$ (not zero, since the tangents exist).

lines.tex: &= \frac{\dfrac{\sin P \cos Q}{\cos P \cos Q} + \dfrac{\cos P \sin Q}{\cos P \cos Q}}{\dfrac{\cos P \cos Q}{\cos P \cos Q} - \dfrac{\sin P \sin Q}{\cos P \cos Q}}

lines.text: $\dfrac{\sin P}{\cos P} = \tan P$ and $\dfrac{\sin Q}{\cos Q} = \tan Q$.
So $\tan(P+Q) = \dfrac{\tan P + \tan Q}{1 - \tan P \tan Q}$, as required.

candidates.question:
Find the exact value of $\cos 210^\circ$.
Give your answer in surd form.

lines.text: $210^\circ$ is in the third quadrant.
Cosine is negative in the third quadrant.
So $I(6) < I(5)$. The tree grew less in year 6 than in year 5: it is still growing, but more slowly.
